content.title: About
content.content: Dried egg yolk is the dehydrated yolk of a chicken egg, obtained by spray‑drying or freeze‑drying. It retains most of the nutrients of fresh yolk, has a long shelf life, and is convenient for the food industry.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Often used in confectionery, sauces, and sports nutrition products.
Freeze‑drying preserves over 90 % of vitamins and minerals compared with conventional drying.
One gram of dried yolk provides roughly 3 g of protein and 30 µg of vitamin D.
It dissolves easily in water, milk, or oil, forming a smooth emulsion.
Serves as a stable substitute for fresh yolk in recipes requiring long storage.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12, riboflavin (B2) and folate, which support energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Source of lecithin
items.content: Lecithin aids fat emulsification and is beneficial for liver and brain function.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Yolk protein provides all essential amino acids, supporting tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Mineral dense
items.content: Provides iron, phosphorus, selenium and zinc, important for immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Suitable for low‑carb diets and athletic nutrition.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: People allergic to eggs may react to dried yolk, potentially experiencing severe reactions.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Yolk contains cholesterol; individuals with high cholesterol should monitor intake.

items.title: Raw material quality
items.content: Poor‑quality raw eggs can harbor bacteria, so source the product from reputable suppliers.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Add dried yolk to doughs, sauces, mayonnaise, protein shakes, and dry baking mixes. To reconstitute, dissolve 1 g of dried yolk in 3 ml of water or milk, let stand 5–10 minutes for hydration.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Shelf life is up to 12 months when unopened; after opening, use within 3 months and check for off‑odors.
